assets.name: 01-overview
assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: publication figure for the English robotics paper RoboRAG.
Primary request: polish the supplied scientific diagram into an elegant Nature-style research figure, preserving its scientific content. This is an EDIT of the input diagram, not a new scientific concept.
Style: exceptionally clear, flat vector-like scientific schematic on pure white; restrained editorial design; dark charcoal text, desaturated navy and teal for main processes, muted burnt orange only for failures/recovery/curation; very pale tinted panels. Fine consistent line weights, clean small arrowheads, generous whitespace, precise alignment, Helvetica/Arial-like typography, subtle corner rounding only if helpful. No gradients, shadows, glossy effects, decorative backgrounds, logos or watermarks. Use panel letters a, b, c where sensible, with short sentence-case headings. Avoid heavy boxed presentation styling. Typography must be legible in a full-width two-column journal figure.
Layout: landscape approximately 2.2:1, high resolution suitable for publication. Keep all diagram content inside generous safe margins. Improve hierarchy and route arrows away from text. Keep each original node and its text legible; concise heading capitalization may change but scientific labels, predicates, IDs, intervals, AND/OR semantics, direction and types of edges must not change. Do not merge graph nodes into object icons. Tiny scientifically neutral line icons are optional only if they improve comprehension without replacing text.
Constraints: reproduce English text correctly, no invented measurements or results; no altered mathematical meanings. Preserve the distinction between solid, dashed and dotted arrows. The supplied image is the edit target and semantic reference. Output ONLY the polished figure artwork, not a page, caption or mockup.

Figure 1: overview. Two clear horizontal bands, training-bank construction above and unseen-task planning/execution below. Preserve all eleven nodes and arrows.
Top: TRAIN episodes (observations, actions and feedback) -> Segment + annotate (check evidence and graph schema) -> Graph bank B (whole graphs + phase subgraphs).
Main: NEW task (goal + observation + capabilities) -> Draft graph plan (roles, conditions, unknowns explicit) -> Retrieve + align (edit + validate; adapted plan P) -> Follow plan (supervisor + local executor) -> Backend (robot / simulator).
Graph bank B feeds Retrieve + align, arrow labeled retrieve.
Backend -> Execution graph X (actual events + evidence), with 'receipts + observations' alongside that elbow arrow, not overlapping it.
Execution graph X -> Planner revision (only when needed; new plan version) -> Retrieve + align (replan). Execution graph X -> Follow plan (status).
Backend -> Separate curation (new bank version after evaluation) -> Graph bank B, BOTH return arrows dashed, upper return labeled reviewed experience. This is separate curation, not test-time leakage. Preserve the distinction between experience graphs, predicted plan P, and observed graph X.
Design the curation return as a quiet dashed upper rail. Main emphasis on graph bank and adapted plan, with executor and observations clearly connected. Do not change these connections.

v3: grasp attempt / [3, 5] s / holding verified

A separate dashed recovery arrow from v1 to v2 ABOVE the chain, labeled 'recovery: failure to reobservation'. It MUST land on v2, never v3.
A separate dotted dependency arrow from v3 to v4 BELOW the chain, labeled 'dependency: holding(item) = true'.
Below the chain arrange two neatly typeset panels.
Left exact record:
Example record for v1
role: grasp(item)     binding: item = cup_7
precondition: reachable(item)
intended effect: holding(item)
observed outcome: failed; evidence = frames_18_21
source: TRAIN episode_12; interval = [0, 2] s
Right exact rules:
Ready to start a phase?
An eligible branch is selected (OR)
AND every prerequisite is true
AND resources are available
Unknown condition: observe first
Requested effect is not completion
Heading: Illustrative observed graph: four distinct phase instances.
Visual emphasis: v1 orange failure, v3 muted teal verified holding, other nodes neutral. Record should feel like a compact scientific data record, not a code screenshot. Recovery and dependency must remain visually distinct. Times and evidence are illustrative schema examples.

Figure 3: retrieval and plan adaptation, three clearly aligned tiers.
Top three inputs:
TRAIN subgraph A: transfer / grasp -> move -> place / item / target roles / failure -> observe -> retry
TRAIN subgraph B: open / approach(handle) -> pull(drawer) / verify open(drawer)
UNSEEN composition / put cup in closed drawer / current cup / handle / drawer
All three input panels point to middle 'ALIGN + EDIT + VALIDATE', with
'item = current cup; target = current drawer'
'insert opening prerequisite; ground geometry; check capabilities'.
Middle points ONLY to the start of the validated plan, with an arrow labeled validated plan.
Bottom plan left to right:
Open drawer / verify open(drawer) / release handle
-> Grasp cup / verify holding(cup)
-> Move cup / check live geometry
-> Place cup / verify in(cup, drawer).
Grasp cup -> Move cup arrow labeled holding.
Failure branch: dashed arrow DOWN from Grasp cup to Reobserve + retry / approved budget only / new attempt ID, labeled failed. Title: Retrieve compatible subgraphs; adapt their conditions and structure.
Optional small neutral line-art cup/drawer motifs may support panels but preserve every word and avoid clutter. Muted teal for adaptation, orange dashed recovery. Use open whitespace between tiers and keep all arrows in gutters. This is an illustrative proposed mechanism, no success rates or results.
